submission.justification: Absorber-F2 at 5mm plate thickness is recommended. While Absorber-F1 at 4mm would provide better energy resolution (3.054%), the hands-on maintenance constraint is critical for safe operation and detector access during shutdowns. Absorber-F2 is explicitly described as a "standard structural absorber," which in collider detector terminology indicates materials (typically steel/iron-based) specifically chosen for their compatibility with hands-on maintenance due to minimal long-lived activation products. Absorber-F1, described as a "dense alloy with a short radiation length," likely contains tungsten which is known to develop long-lived radioactive isotopes that prevent hands-on maintenance. At 5mm thickness, F2 achieves its optimal energy resolution of 4.888%, which represents the best performance achievable while meeting the mandatory safety constraint. All materials can be machined to required tolerances and are compatible with the mechanical support design.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 is one of the three candidate materials listed in candidate_specs.md

requirements.requirement: Must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 is described as 'standard structural absorber' which indicates materials specifically chosen for hands-on maintenance compatibility in collider detectors, unlike dense alloys (F1, F3) which may have activation concerns
Recommended thickness of 5mm is within the specified range of 2-10mm

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Among materials that meet the hands-on maintenance constraint, F2 at 5mm achieves optimal resolution of 4.888% at 100 GeV (tested range 2-10mm). While F1 offers better resolution (3.054% at 4mm), it likely cannot meet the mandatory maintenance constraint due to activation concerns typical of tungsten-based dense alloys.
